name: White Salmon Glacier
approach: From the small pull-off at the old White Salmon Lodge on the Mount Baker Highway, walk around the gate and follow the old road past the lodge site for about a mile to where it ends at an old clearcut. With good snow cover, descend northeast to White Salmon Creek and follow the valley up to the toe of the White Salmon Glacier. Without it, hold your height through the clearcut and contour, losing elevation only to get around rock bands and stream crossings, to stay out of the slide alder in the valley bottom. Bivy sites sit among the rock outcrops along the eastern edge of the glacier.
firstResearcherNote: Added the lower White Salmon bivy, which was missing; elevation omitted as not confirmed.

name: South Corner

Bear onto the Flapjack Lakes Trail, which climbs steadily and then steeply (with one rough slide/washout bypass to pick through) for roughly 3.4-4.1 more miles, gaining about 2,000 ft, to reach Flapjack Lakes (~3,850 ft, about 7.5-8 miles from the …

name: Standard Scramble

Expect significant brush and blowdowns low, easier scrambling higher up.
firstResearcherNote: Lake Sundown is the usual base; unsure exactly where the Belview/Six Ridge camps fall relative to the Olson way, kept as on-route since they are on the same ridge trail.

firstResearcherNote: The Lichtenhorn stands over Lake Valhalla, the natural camp; unsure this rarely climbed line is ever done overnight.

name: South Slopes Scramble
approach: Park at the Yodelin lot on US 2 (the former Yodelin ski area's lot, now used for overflow parking, roughly 1.7 miles from the Stevens Pass Ski Area pedestrian overpass, around milepost 60). Cross the highway and follow the old ski-area road south into the valley, staying near Nason Creek where crossings/snow bridges are most reliable, then continue into the open basin below the Spinnaker-Tye Peak ridge before turning up to the gap below Point 5261.
firstResearcherNote: Rarely climbed; the Tye-Spinnaker basin is mainly a winter camp and summer parties likely do it in a day. Waypoint basin entry dropped as a duplicate. Unsure whether the basin is inside a wilderness.

The standard SE-slope scramble route is reached via Upper Thunder Mountain Lake.

name: Southeast Ridge
approach: Start at the Beverly Turnpike Trailhead at the end of FR-9737-112 (roughly 3,650 ft). At about 0.5 mile, bear left onto signed Trail #1391 (Beverly Turnpike/Beverly Creek Trail) — do not miss this junction, as a wrong-fork error onto the Bean Creek Trail is a commonly reported mistake. Continue to roughly 3.1 miles and turn right onto Trail #1226.1 (Fourth Creek Trail), climbing to Fourth Creek Pass at about 3.6 miles (roughly 5,900-6,000 ft), which opens up the first real views of Argonaut, Colchuck, and Dragontail. Snow is typically encountered around 4,700 ft; continue to the base of the north face couloir.

The path is unmaintained and can be hard to follow.
